messages.subject: latent growth curve correlation
parts:
Good evening kind colleagues, 
I would like to find the relationship between the 4 latent slopes net of the other predictor variables, so I thought I would calculate the correlation between them in a multivariate regerssion model.
 
In model 1, following the guide of http://web.pdx.edu/~newsomj/semclass/ho_growth%20second%20example.pdf
I created all the latent slopes I am interested in (15 variables, 4 will be used as dependent covariates and the others used as predictors), and I created a new database with the predicted slopes.

I standardized all slopes (centered on the mean and divided by their own standard deviation) in order to compare their effect sizes in the regression.

With model 2 (multilevel) I would like to estimate the effects on the 4 dependents and calculate the correlation between them. 
model2="
level: 1
sMAP~sCSability + sCSopinion + sAutoReg ....
sPAP~sCSability + sCSopinion + sAutoReg ....
sMAV~sCSability + sCSopinion + sAutoReg ....
sPAV~sCSability + sCSopinion + sAutoReg ....
level: 2
sMAP~1
sPAP~1
sMAV~1
sPAV~1
"

At this point, how do I extract the correlations I am looking for between the 4 slopes? 
I think standardized covariance is what I'm looking for.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: latent growth curve correlation
parts: the relationship between the 4 latent slopes net of the other predictor variables

Does "net" mean you want their residual/partial correlation matrix?

lavInspect(fit, "est")$psi

If you want the model-implied marginal (zero-order, "total") correlation matrix:

lavInspect(fit, "cor.lv")
I think standardized covariance is what I'm looking for.

The "Std.all" column provides the residual/partial correlations.
